claim: A beat that follows a big run into the print gets sold on the reaction
test: 2-day post-earnings return on names up 8%+ in the 5 sessions before the print. Pattern fails if those names hold or extend the gain.

instances.detail: Up ~8% into the print, beat consensus, then -8.0% after hours to 478.05, below its entire regular-session low
EPS -0.09 vs -0.16 est (beat), ran +9.92% on 2x volume, gave the entire move back after hours to 115.98

Third instance, next-day confirmation. Beat revenue (11.5B, +50% y/y), data center +107% to 6.72B, EPS 1.66 vs 1.55 est. Ran ~8% INTO the print. Gross margin missed 54% vs 56% and it fell 8.8% pre-market to 472.90 against a 518.58 close. The Bench passed on the pre-print bet for exactly this reason.

claim: 7-day verdicts invert; 30 days is the first checkpoint worth publishing
test: Compare the 1w and 1m verdict on the same archive row. Pattern fails if sign flips are rare (<10% of scored rows).

instances.detail: Scored WRONG at 1w (-0.72%), RIGHT at 1m (+11.64%, alpha +11.34). Sign flipped.
+4.7% at 1w became +21.46% at 1m. Same verdict, wildly different magnitude.

claim: Relative volume, not percent move, identifies a real repricing in a crowded up-tape
test: On scan days, check whether the name with rel-vol >1.0 kept its move while bigger percent movers on sub-1.0 volume faded.

instances.detail: Only row of 49 in the broad scan with rel-vol >1.0 (2.9x). Fell -20.2% and held it, while MU +7.7%, SMCI +10.5%, AMD +8.5% all ran on sub-1.1x and faded

claim: A float under ~10% of shares outstanding means price is set by supply, not by the business
test: Track low-float names against their own earnings: pattern fails if fundamentals move price more than lockup/supply events do.

instances.detail: Float 646M of 14.02B shares = 4.6%. Beat earnings and sold anyway; -48.6% from the June high on no fundamental break

Supply flow set every turn of the last two weeks with zero business news: 52wk low 104.83 printed Aug 3, THREE sessions BEFORE the Aug 6 first-lockup expiry (~911.5M shares), then +32% off the low through the unlock to 139.98, and today the first red day arrived on no catalyst at all - rejected 139.98, closed 133.36, -3.88% on 108.9M vs 99.3M 30d avg. Sell-the-rumor-buy-the-news into a dated supply event, both directions. Data-integrity note: shares outstanding feed now reads 16.07B vs 13.31B yesterday vs 14.02B Aug 4, float still stuck at 646M - the float/SO math is unusable, but the price behavior alone carries the instance.

claim: A stop run by a thesis-level news event should not be re-entered on the same-day bounce
test: Track re-entries after news-driven stop-outs: measure the 5-day return from the bounce price vs the stop price. Pattern fails if re-entering on the bounce beats waiting.

instances.detail: Stop filled 357.00 on the DeepMind exodus. Bounce to ~365 on volume fading 3.0M -> 753K. Re-entry declined; outcome to be graded at 30 days.

claim: A beat on the quarter gets sold anyway when forward guidance softens - the guide outranks the print
test: Track the 2-day post-earnings return for names that beat on BOTH revenue and EPS but cut, softened, or missed on forward guidance. Pattern fails if those names hold or extend.

instances.detail: Adjusted EPS beat 0.49 vs 0.38. FY revenue guide CUT to 3.56B from 3.59B. Closed -20.2% on 2.9x volume, at day lows.
Beat revenue 11.5B +50%, EPS 1.66 vs 1.55, data center +107%. Gross margin 54% vs 56% consensus with Helios ramp costs flagged. -8.8% premarket, closed -7.1%.

Beat revenue 802M +23.5%, adj EPS 1.66 +41.5%, adj gross margin 72.9% +320bps. Cut US Omnipod growth to 17-19% and previewed 2027 mid-teens on type-2 dropoff. Closed -20.2% on 5.5x volume, fresh 52wk low 126.50.

Insulet beat Q2 (rev $802M +23.5%, adj EPS $1.66 +41.5%, gross margin +320bps) and closed -20.2% on 5.5x average volume. Sold entirely on the forward guide: US Omnipod cut to 17-19% and a preliminary 2027 view exiting in the mid-teens, on type 2 retention loss inside the first 90 days. Second instance same session as AMD, unrelated sector - falsification would be a beat-plus-soft-guide that closes green on above-average volume.

Cleanest instance yet. EPS BEAT (CHF 0.31 vs 0.29) but revenue MISSED (CHF 850.3M vs 881.4M consensus) and FY26 sales-growth guidance was CUT to low-20% from 'at least 23%', with Americas - over half of sales - decelerating to +13% cc from +17% in Q1 on a 'highly promotional U.S. market'. Closed -20.29% at 30.91 on 43.76M shares vs a 4.18M 30-day average (10.5x), a fresh 52-week low of 30.1122 and the steepest single-day drop since its 2021 IPO. Peers barely moved (NKE -1.96%, DECK -3.72%), confirming company-specific rejection of the guide, not a sector move. DTC +34.3% cc beat everywhere and did not save it - the forward number outranked every good line in the print.

Rev beat 9.95B vs 9.67B est, but Q4 EPS guided 2.05-2.25 vs street 2.36 (handsets -20% y/y, memory-cost margin squeeze). Sold -4.4% to 155.68 and gapped down next day to 146.55 low 146.00. Guide outranked the beat exactly as claimed. Notable coda: entire gap reclaimed by 8/13 on below-avg volume.

claim: The 5-session run INTO the print sets the reaction; beat-vs-miss barely matters
test: For names up 8%+ in the 5 sessions before a print, track 2-day post-earnings return SPLIT BY beat/in-line/miss. Pattern fails if the beat/miss split explains more of the reaction variance than the run does, or if 8%+ runners hold their gains regardless of outcome.

instances.detail: Ran +20.6% in the 5 sessions into the print, then MISSED badly (-0.66 vs -0.21 est). D+1 -11.6%, D+2 -9.4%. Sold hard.
Ran +9.7% into the print, MISSED (-0.20 vs -0.14 est). D+1 -2.2%, D+2 -3.4%, D+5 -9.4%.

CONTROL/no-run case: DOWN 10.6% in the 5 sessions before the print, MISSED by the widest margin of the set (-0.41 vs -0.12 est), and rallied D+1 +8.4%, D+2 +9.0%. Worst miss, best reaction - because there was no run to unwind.

claim: When the reported quarter and the forward guide point OPPOSITE ways, the reaction follows the GUIDE
test: Find names where the reported quarter and the forward guide disagree in direction (miss + raise, or beat + cut). Track the 2-day post-earnings return. Pattern FAILS if the reaction follows the reported beat/miss instead of the guide, or if such names go flat.

instances.detail: BEAT EPS (CHF 0.31 vs 0.29) and MISSED revenue (850.3M vs 881.4M), then CUT FY26 sales growth to low-20% from 'at least 23%' with Americas - over half of sales - slowing to +13% cc from +17%. Reaction followed the GUIDE, not the EPS beat: -20.29% to 30.91 on 10.5x volume, fresh 52wk low, worst day since the 2021 IPO.

MIRROR CASE, SAME SESSION. MISSED revenue (11.1B vs 11.551B expected) and beat EPS hard (1.62 vs 0.96), then RAISED FY27 sales guidance to 65-72B against a 52.5B consensus (+24% to +37% above street), Q1 FY27 sales 14.5-15.5B vs 11.68B, and reported gross margin 15-17% against 8.2-8.4% guided on favourable AI-system mix. Reaction followed the GUIDE, not the revenue miss: +9.41% to 34.42 post-market. Paired with ONON on the same day this isolates the variable - identical print shape (EPS beat + revenue miss), opposite guides, 30 points of reaction apart.

D+1 confirmation of the Aug 11 mirror case. The +9.41% post-market reaction to the guide (FY27 65-72B vs 52.5B street) EXTENDED to +18.85% at the D+1 close: 31.60 -> 37.56 on the regular session, holding ~37.27 after hours. The guide-following reaction did not fade at the open - it doubled. Two-day test window closes tomorrow; as of D+1 the reaction followed the guide, not the revenue miss, in full.

GDS missed Q2 EPS by 61% (0.52 actual vs 1.35 est) and CLOSED +6.72% at 34.94 on 5.05M shares vs a 1.65M 30-day average = 3.05x relative volume. The guide is the entire move: FY26 revenue guidance RAISED from RMB12.4-12.9B to RMB12.7-13.0B, and the full-year bookings target DOUBLED from 500MW to 1GW, with H1 bookings at a record 470MW, 600MW of additional customer reservations, binding commitments now above 2GW, and capex guidance raised RMB9B to RMB10B. Net income RMB837.6M vs a RMB70.6M LOSS a year ago. Quarter and guide pointed opposite ways and the reaction followed the GUIDE - 4th instance, and the first one measured on 3x relative volume, which per P-003 marks it as a real institutional repricing rather than a retail bounce. Verified via GlobeNewswire release and the SEC 6-K exhibit.

FIRST FAILURE. Textbook P-008 setup: EPS MISSED by 32c (-0.37 vs -0.05) while the company RAISED FY26 revenue guidance to 3.1-3.3B and guided Q3 to 880-900M, +47-50% YoY. Quarter and guide pointed opposite ways, and the reaction followed the MISS, not the guide: D+1 -3.97% (gapped 31.77 to 29.71), then four consecutive lower closes to 28.16 = -11.4%, losing the 200-day on day three. DISCRIMINATOR vs the SMCI cases that built this pattern: SMCI missed on shipment TIMING while its guide rewrote forward revenue, so the guide was new information. HIMS missed on STRUCTURAL MARGIN - gross margin 63.8% vs 76.4% a year earlier on the compounded-to-branded GLP-1 pivot, six straight quarters of compression, and net income from +42.5M to -86.3M on revenue up 38.2%. When the miss IS the forward economics, the raise gets discounted rather than priced. Candidate refinement for v25, NOT applied on one instance.

PERSISTENCE CHECK, 10 sessions after the 2026-08-11 mirror pair - the guide repricings did NOT mean-revert, which is the objection this pattern most needed answered. SMCI closed 37.56 on 8/12 (D+1, +18.85%) and closed 37.25 on Friday 2026-08-21, holding essentially all of the guide move. ONON closed 30.91 on 8/11 after the FY26 cut and closed 30.03 Friday, still below where the cut left it - it never bounced. Live get_equity_quotes pull 2026-08-23 13:35 CT, last_trade_price at 2026-08-21T19:59:59Z. So the guide does not produce a pop that fades, it reprices the company and the price stays repriced. Falsification for this leg: a P-008 instance whose post-guide move is fully retraced inside 10 sessions on average-or-below volume.

claim: When a leveraged ETF carries higher relative volume than its own cash proxy, the move is retail crowding, not institutional repricing
test: On the day, compare rel-vol of the leveraged vehicle vs its cash proxy/underlying. Pattern holds if the move fades or mean-reverts within 7 sessions while the cash proxy never confirms on above-average volume. FALSIFIED if the cash proxy catches up on volume and the move extends past 7 sessions - that would mean real money followed the leverage in.

claim: A commodity- or rate-linked stock only trades its own earnings if earnings days appear among its ten biggest single-day moves; otherwise the print is the wrong catalyst
test: For the name, rank its ten largest single-day moves over ~18 months and count how many are earnings reaction days, then compare the average absolute earnings-day move to the stock's overall volatility. Pattern HOLDS if names with 2+ earnings days in the top ten move materially on their prints while names with 0-1 do not (their average earnings-day move collapses toward ~2% despite high general ATR). FALSIFIED if a name with 0-1 earnings days in its top ten nevertheless produces repeated large, tradeable earnings reactions.

instances.detail: ZIM: 0 of its 10 biggest single-day moves in 18 months are earnings days. Avg earnings-day move 1.90% despite ATR 3.17%. Its +39.6% move (2/13-2/17) was NOT an earnings date - Q4 printed 3/9. Confirmed by FRO (0/10, avg 3.55%), NAT (1/10, 3.20%) and NMM (0/10, 2.04%). Falsifying controls in the same lane: SFL 4/10 with avg 8.57% and TRMD 2/10 with avg 6.05% - both DO move on their own prints. Six names measured, clean split.

claim: A RAISED guide still gets sold when the economics underneath it deteriorate - margins compressing, losses widening, or the raise carried by a lumpy line while the recurring line stalls
test: On any raise-and-fall, read the release for (a) gross margin or EBITDA moving the WRONG way in the same quarter, or (b) the raise carried by a non-recurring line item while the recurring one is flat. Pattern HOLDS if at least one is present and the stock fell. FALSIFIED if a company raises guidance WITH improving margins AND improving recurring revenue and is still sold off - that would mean something other than unit economics is doing the work. This refines the v24 Guide Rule rather than contradicting it: the guide outranks the print, but the line items underneath outrank the guide.

instances.detail: Reported 8/13 BEFORE THE OPEN. Revenue 83.8M vs ~68M est - a 23% BEAT, up more than 13-fold y/y - and FY26 revenue guidance RAISED to 525-550M, roughly 10x prior expectations. CEO cited sustained momentum. Stock CLOSED -8.80% at 8.91 on 106M+ shares. What was moving the wrong way in the same release: adjusted EBITDA loss WIDENED to 50.6M, gross margin DECLINED to 43.1%, and EPS MISSED at -0.19 vs -0.07 est. Valuation carried none of it - EV/Revenue 40, forward P/S above 10 even on 2027. Peers barely moved (AVAV -2.27%, KTOS -1.66%, RCAT -0.97%, UMAC +0.81%) on a green tape (SPY +0.68%), so this was idiosyncratic at 4-9x peer magnitude, not sector beta. A 10x guidance raise could not outrank a widening loss and a compressing margin.

Raised FY26 revenue growth guidance from 12% to 13-15% and still fell 17.5% the same day (38.67 to 31.92). The raise was carried entirely by the LUMPY line: licensing +21% y/y, its strongest licensing quarter in three years, while ROYALTIES - the recurring annuity for an IP licensor - went essentially FLAT at +1% y/y. Surfaced by the guide-verification scout on 8/13. The market repriced the timing of the royalty inflection out to 2027 and charged for the wait. Distinguishing evidence: CEVA is the only name of five in that scan that NEVER bounced - three consecutive sessions of continued bleed (31.92, 30.83, 30.44, 30.60), so this was a sustained repricing rather than a one-day overreaction.

Beat both lines (rev 9.115B vs 9.00B, EPS 3.50 vs 3.39) AND guided Q4 far above street (rev 10.25B +/-0.5B vs 9.54B consensus, EPS 4.02 +/-0.20 vs 3.65) - and was sold anyway: -2.30% into the 8/13 close off a 563.76 high, -5.18% after hours, ~-5.7% premarket 8/14 at ~504. The deteriorating line underneath: Q4 gross-margin guide FLAT sequentially despite +12% sequential revenue, blamed on ramp costs and a higher mix of lower-margin display revenue, plus China revenue still shrinking. Second beat-plus-raise sold in 24 hours (CSCO -8.35% on 2.95x volume 8/13, margins unexamined so not logged). Entry context: +108% YTD into the print. Third instance, second consecutive day.

claim: The AI trade splits on CASH EARNINGS NOW versus CAPEX MONETIZED LATER. As FY2027 numbers arrive, names whose multiple rests on future monetization get repriced down, while AI names already converting to earnings hold or re-rate up. Adam's call, 2026-08-14: 'the ai run has been a lot of speculation, I see next years earning wrecking some'
test: Split the AI complex into two baskets at logging: (A) EARNINGS-BACKED - positive FCF and a trailing PE under ~25 today (GOOGL 17.26 is the anchor); (B) STORY-PRICED - negative FCF, no PE, or a multiple resting on announced capex and bookings rather than delivered profit. Track the 2-day post-earnings reaction and the trailing 4-quarter return of both baskets across the FY2027 reporting cycle (roughly Q4-26 prints in Jan-2027 through Q3-27 prints in Oct-2027). PATTERN HOLDS if basket B's median post-print reaction is materially negative while basket A's is flat-to-positive, and the A-minus-B return spread is positive. PATTERN FAILS if basket B holds or extends, if the spread is flat or negative, or if the drawdown is INDISCRIMINATE - an everything-selloff that takes A down with B is a macro event, NOT this pattern, and must be recorded as holds=false. Related and already supported: P-006 and P-008 (the guide outranks the print) are the single-name mechanism this basket-level claim would operate through.

claim: Every closed swing in this book has exited at its STOP; not one has ever reached Target 1. A 1.0-1.1 ATR stop is a one-to-three-day stop, not a two-to-eight-week stop, so the framework's own default holding window and its own minimum stop distance are in structural conflict.
test: For each closed swing, record (a) whether the exit was the stop or a target, and (b) the holding period in sessions against the 2-8 week default window. The pattern FAILS the moment a trade exits at T1 or T2, or the moment a stop at or near 1.0 ATR survives a full four-week hold.

instances.detail: Stop 1.064 ATR from basis. Entered 34.40 on 8/18 8:49:34a, stopped 32.60 on 8/19 8:50:26a. Held 24 hours 52 seconds against a 2-8 week intended window. T1 37.85 never approached; best print was 35.045, which is 7.4% short of target. Exit was the stop.

Stop ratcheted to 0.11 ATR (the B-113 case that earned the v25 ATR Floor). Entered 29.145 on 8/11, stopped 29.29 on 8/17. Held 6 sessions against a 2-8 week window. T1 32.80 never paid; best print 31.30, 4.6% short. Exit was the stop. Stock is 30.245 today, 3.3% ABOVE the stop - the one genuine case where the stop cost money.

Entered 332.38 on 7/30, exited 357.00 on 8/5 via a RATCHETED TRAILING stop, +24.62 = +7.41%. Held 6 sessions against a 2-8 week window. Still an exit at the stop rather than at a target - but the honest note is that the trailing stop CAPTURED the gain here rather than cutting it, and GOOGL is 345.45 today, 3.2% BELOW the exit. Holding would have made 11.55 LESS. This instance holds on mechanism (stop, not target) while cutting against the idea that stops are the problem.

COUNTERFACTUAL RUN 8/19 REFUTES THE HYPOTHESIS ON THIS INSTANCE. P-013 claims a 1.0-1.1 ATR stop is too tight for a multi-week hold. HPQ's ORIGINAL stop was 27.65 = 1.09 ATR and was NEVER HIT - the lowest print across the whole holding period was 28.305 on 8/12, leaving 0.39 ATR of clearance at the worst moment. A hypothetical 1.0 ATR stop at 27.771 also survives. What killed the trade was the RATCHET to 29.30 (0.11 ATR), not the stop distance. Without the ratchet the position is open today at 30.245 = +16.50 instead of +2.17. The 1.0 ATR floor was sufficient here; the ratchet rule was not.

COUNTERFACTUAL RUN 8/19 ALSO REFUTES THE FIX ON THIS INSTANCE. A 2.0 ATR stop would sit at 31.02 (34.40 basis, ATR 1.6916) and would NOT have been hit - the lowest print since entry is ~32.55. But the position would simply still be OPEN and losing: marked 32.70 = -27.20 against a realized -28.80. The wider stop buys 1.60 and an unresolved loser. Widening the ATR Floor does not rescue this trade, so this instance cuts against the proposed remedy even though the underlying observation (exited at the stop, never reached T1) still holds.
